## 2025-02-28 - Preventing XSS in Rich Text Rendering
**Vulnerability:** The application stores blog post content as rich HTML generated by the admin `BlogEditor`. However, in `BlogPostPage.tsx`, it was originally rendering this content directly in `{post.content}`, which would incorrectly display HTML tags as plain text, while `BlogEditor.tsx` used `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the live preview without sanitizing the input. This combination of unsafe rendering and direct HTML embedding posed a risk of Stored XSS vulnerabilities.
**Learning:** React's `{}` escapes strings to prevent XSS, but to render actual HTML structure (which a rich text editor produces), you must use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Bypassing React's escaping mechanism safely requires sanitization via tools like DOMPurify. Additionally, fallback strings with classes need to use standard HTML `class` instead of `className` when passed to `DOMPurify.sanitize()` because DOMPurify parses it as standard HTML and will strip React-specific attributes.
**Prevention:** Always wrap variables representing user-generated HTML in `DOMPurify.sanitize()` before passing them to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Ensure fallback HTML structures use standard HTML attributes.
